blurb:
China Great Wall on Sandy Plains Rd is the kind of neighborhood Chinese spot that just gets the job done. Strip mall location, familiar menu, no surprises. When I want lo mein or General Tso's on a Tuesday night without driving far or spending much, this is where I go. Good for a quick weeknight dinner or an easy takeout run.

The menu covers all the classics you'd expect. Nothing on there is going to shock you, but the food comes out solid and the portions are fair for the price. If you've got picky eaters at home who want something reliable, this fits the bill.

Sunday hours start at 3pm, so don't plan on an early afternoon pickup that day.

blurb:
When my kids are in the mood for something different and nobody can agree on what to eat, Pacific Buffet on Chastain Meadows Pkwy is usually where we land. It's all-you-can-eat, so everyone gets what they want without an argument. Good for a casual family dinner when you just want to eat and not think too hard about it.

The sushi and tempura are the reasons most people keep coming back. Nothing fancy, but both are solid for a buffet. My wife goes straight for the sushi line. I tend to work through the tempura and whatever hot entrees look good that day.

At this price point, expectations matter. Come for the variety and the value, not for a gourmet experience. With over 4,200 reviews sitting at 4.1 stars, people clearly keep coming back.

blurb:
The Wing Cafe on Roswell Rd is where you go when you want wings, cold beer, and some actual energy in the room. It's got a tiki bar out back with live music on weekends. My wife and I have gone on a Friday night and stayed way longer than we planned, which I think is the best thing a bar can do to you.

The wings are the whole point, and they hold up. Good craft beer selection to go with them. This is a solid game-day spot or a casual Friday night out with friends where nobody is trying too hard.

They're open seven days a week until 11pm, so it works for a late dinner too if that's your situation.

blurb:
If you want a seafood dinner that actually feels like an event, Marietta Fish Market on Canton Rd delivers. The place is big, loud, and has this whole dramatic ocean-themed thing going on inside. It sounds cheesy but somehow works. My wife and I have brought family there a few times when we needed somewhere that could handle a big group without anyone leaving hungry. The portions are not messing around.

Seafood is the move here, and the plates are generous. This is the kind of place where you're probably leaving with a to-go box regardless of how hungry you walked in. If you're into fried seafood platters or just want a lot of food for a reasonable price, you'll be happy.

They're closed Mondays, so plan around that. Weekend crowds can get big given they're one of the more popular seafood spots in the area, so if you're going Saturday night, factor in some wait time.

blurb:
This one is a legit hidden gem. Los Amigos on Allgood Rd is a Mexican grocery store with a taqueria in the back, and if you sleep on it because of that, you're making a mistake. I brought my wife there on a whim and we were both caught off guard by how good the food actually is.

The pastor torta is what you need to order. The meat is seasoned well, not overcooked, not too crispy. Just right. The pupusas are also worth getting, specifically the bean and cheese. And the chicken plate with rice and beans is the real deal, the kind where you can tell the chicken was marinated overnight, not just thrown on a grill. Homemade beans too, not from a can.

Thursday hours cut off earlier than the rest of the week, so if Thursday is your night, plan to go before 7pm.
